title: Follow-up Actions After NParks-funded Study on Feral Pigeons
what_it_is: Follow-up Actions After NParks-funded Study on Feral Pigeons

sections.label: NParks feral pigeon study actions
sections.summary: NParks' population management for wild birds includes food source reduction, habitat modification, population control, food waste management, enforcement, and the 2021 "Say No to Feeding Wildlife" campaign.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether NParks will be taking any follow-up actions following an NParks-funded study titled “Restricted human activities shift the foraging strategies of feral pigeons (Columba livia) and three other commensal bird species”; and (b) if so, what are these actions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: These findings have highlighted the importance of food source reduction, which are part of NParks’ population management measures for wild birds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: This is multi-pronged, including habitat modification and population control.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: To reduce the availability of food sources, NParks has been working closely with the Singapore Food Agency, National Environment Agency and Town Councils to encourage proper food waste management at food establishments and to enforce against littering and illegal bird-feeding.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: As part of its outreach and education efforts, NParks launched the islandwide “Say No to Feeding Wildlife” campaign in January 2021 to raise awareness on the negative impact of feeding wildlife, including birds.
